title: Response Guarantee Credit Terms — Commercial & Property Manager Service Agreements
content:
**Terms.** The agreement must be in active status on the dispatch date of the job an SLA credit is claimed for. When the crew's recorded arrival on an emergency water or fire job of the customer exceeds the agreement's response commitment, the agreement earns the tier's SLA credit for that job, at most the tier's maximum credits per job and never more than the tier's SLA credit cap per term in total. An SLA credit may be posted only when the customer claims it no later than the SLA claim window after the late dispatch. The SLA claim window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the late job's opened date, and a claim made on the last day of the window is in time. The SLA credit is posted on the agreement; it is separate from, and stacks with, any late-arrival waiver of the service call fee on the job itself.

These terms govern SLA credits under the Commercial & Property Manager Service Agreements.

## When a credit is earned

| Requirement | Where it is shown |
|---|---|
| The job is an emergency water or fire job of the customer | the customer's job record |
| The crew's recorded arrival exceeds the agreement's response commitment | the arrival recorded on that job, against the tier's response commitment |
| The agreement was in active status on the job's dispatch date | the agreement's status on the date the job was opened |
| The customer claims the credit no later than the SLA claim window after the late dispatch | the job's opened date and the date of the claim |

The credit earned is the tier's SLA credit for that job.

## Limits

- **Per job:** at most the tier's maximum credits per job.
- **Per term:** never more than the tier's SLA credit cap per term in total, the total being the SLA credits posted on the agreement within the current term, from its start date through its term end date.

## The claim window

- The clock starts from the late dispatch, as shown by the late job's opened date.
- The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after that opened date, for the tier's SLA claim window days.
- A claim made on the last day of the window is in time; a claim made after the last day is not.

*Boundary illustration (hypothetical dates and window):* with a 30-day window and a late job opened on 3 March, day one of the window is 4 March and the last day is 2 April. A claim made on 2 April is in time; a claim made on 3 April is outside the window.

## Relation to the job's own service call fee

The SLA credit is posted on the agreement. It is separate from, and stacks with, any late-arrival waiver of the service call fee on the job itself: a waiver on the job does not reduce or replace the credit on the agreement.

## Points of judgement

- A late arrival on an emergency water job dispatched on a day the agreement was suspended does not satisfy the status requirement, since the agreement was not in active status on that dispatch date.
- A credit already posted on the agreement for a job leaves no further credit for that job where the tier's maximum credits per job is one.
